findings.summary: The plan does not say where in note_finished the call goes, and the function returns early.
findings.evidence: note_finished returns early when self.nested is set or the state is not Landed or Rejected. The plan only says 'Call the check from note_finished; tick untouched'. If the call goes before that guard, nested runs and failed jobs would also queue requests. If it goes after, hook test (b) has to pass OutcomeState::Landed with nested set to None. Fix: Say that the call goes after the existing guard and before tick. Have hook test (b) use OutcomeState::Landed with a non-nested Athena.

findings.summary: The cadence count is not defined: which records count as a landing, and from which point.
findings.evidence: go() can reach both note_finished and land_pr for one job. The plan dedups by deriving the count from records, but it never says what it counts: landed jobs or landing records, and counted from when the last review request was created or from its id. Fix: State one rule in the module header and in decisions.md. For example: count jobs whose outcome is Landed with a landing time after the creation time of the latest design-review request, or after the baseline. Have the cadence test run both hooks for one job and assert the count goes up by one.

findings.summary: run.rs is listed as a file to modify, but the plan says it may stay unchanged.
findings.evidence: The plan says 'Only if needed for a comment; otherwise unchanged'. The hook goes through note_finished, which run.rs:152 already calls. Fix: Drop run.rs from the files list, or name the exact change it needs.

summary: I read the code the plan depends on, and it is there. Athena::land_pr is at gh.rs:2455. Its Landed-only blocks call resync_onto_merge with ? at line 2575 and then watch_pages at line 2586, so the planned hook goes in the right place. Athena::note_finished is at steward.rs:98 and is called from go at run.rs:152. The test check is named "test" in checks.rs. CheckRun has a duration field (records.rs:731), so the test run time can be read. syn 2.0.119 and proc-macro2 are already in Cargo.lock. Every criterion has a demonstration that would fail without its behavior. The hook tests name the exact count of 2, treat zero tests run as a failure, and are checked against removing each hook call. The first-review baseline follows the reading. No athena.toml field is added, and the work fits one producer run. I found only minor gaps: where the call sits in note_finished relative to its early return, and which landings and states count toward the cadence.
